subject: Archival grace period & backup purge alignment for DPA (proposal)
messages:
From: Acme Health - DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health - Security Ops <security-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: backup purge / archival grace for DPA mapping

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the onboarding call last week. We're running our DPA alignment review and need to confirm how Redwood treats deleted customer data across live systems, backups, and logs. A couple of specific items from our legal and security teams:

- Live-data deletion SLA: we need confirmation that account-level deletion requests remove live data within 30 days and that any retry/repair windows are documented.
- Backups / snapshots: you mentioned a standard 90-day purge window for automated backups. Please confirm whether tenants can request a shorter or longer window, and whether longer windows require a DPA addendum.
- Log retention: our audit team is asking for 180 days for certain access logs for compliance. Is there a formal exception process for logs?
- Subprocessor visibility: provide the subprocessor list for storage/backups and whether subprocessor changes trigger notice.

I've attached a short memo with our DPO's bullets and an anonymized list of required evidence items. Can you send a proposed path for how we get a documented exception (if needed) or an addendum we can sign?

Appreciate a short plan and timeline — we need to present to procurement by Oct 12.

Regards,
Lena Marsh
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

Attachment: acme-dpo-retention-questions.pdf

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Health - DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Acme Health - Security Ops <security-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: backup purge / archival grace for DPA mapping

Lena — thanks, and great questions. I pulled together a short proposal so procurement/legal has an actionable option ahead of your Oct 12 review. High level:

- Live-data deletion: Redwood confirms live tenant data is removed from primary stores within 30 calendar days of an approved deletion request. We maintain a 30-day change buffer for ongoing jobs; we log state transitions and provide a deletion confirmation report.

- Backups & snapshots (current default): automated incremental backups are kept for 90 days and then purged. Cold snapshots (manual/exported) are retained up to 1 year by default for troubleshooting and interventions.

- Proposed option for Acme: offer a scoped backup-retention SLA of 120 days for account ACME-12345 (we can shorten on request). Longer retention (beyond 1 year) requires a DPA addendum and explicit KMS scoping.

- Log retention exceptions: we can supply a formal exception workflow. For audit-critical logs (security/access), we can permit up to 180 days on a per-account basis with reviewer approvals from Legal + Security and a documented retention waiver in the account file.

I'll loop in Legal to draft a DPA addendum and the exception template. Attached is our internal proposed backup SLA spreadsheet showing the purge cadence and options.

Next steps I propose: 1) Kimberly review DPA addendum draft, 2) sign addendum if Acme accepts 120d SLA + 180d logs waiver, 3) vendor verification for subprocessor list and KMS hold.

I attached our proposed schedule (redwood-proposed-backup-sla.xlsx). If that aligns, I can push a DocuSign for signature next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposed-backup-sla.xlsx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Acme Health - DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: backup purge / archival grace for DPA mapping

Vanessa / Lena — quick legal note from our side. We can accommodate a customer-specific backup retention SLA with a DPA addendum. A few clarifications we need captured in the addendum:

- Scope: define whether the retention applies to automated incremental backups only, or to cold/manual snapshots and exports as well. Our recommended language is to limit to automated backups and list cold snapshots as an optional, separately billed archival service.
- Security controls: for retention beyond 90 days we require KMS-managed keys scoped to the tenant and audit logs for any key access. Please confirm Acme will accept KMS constraints.
- Subprocessor notices: we will provide the current subprocessor list (storage + observability) and commit to 30 days notice for material changes affecting backups.
- Evidence: for SOC 2 / retention proof, we can provide a quarterly export of deletion logs and a signed purge manifest.

I've created a draft addendum for your review — it includes a 120-day backup SLA and a clause for a 180-day log-waiver subject to mutual sign-off. See attached. If Acme signs, Legal will run a short internal risk review and trigger our vendor confirmation with CloudOps (they will provide subprocessor attestations).

Attachment: dpa-addendum-backup-retention-draft.docx

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Health - DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-ops@acmehealth.com, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: backup purge / archival grace for DPA mapping

Hi Kimberly and Vanessa,

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the draft addendum. Acme is generally okay with the 120-day automated backup SLA. A couple of additional asks from procurement/security before signature:

1) Log-waiver: we need the 180-day log retention clause to be explicit about which log types (access, admin, API request traces) and include an audit trigger clause (Redwood to notify Acme within 10 business days of any anomaly affecting log integrity).
2) Subprocessor attestation: please have CloudOps provide a signed attestation (email is fine) that backups for ACME-12345 are stored in the us-east-1 region and encrypted with a tenant-specific KMS key.
3) Purge manifest cadence: we prefer a monthly purge-manifest export for the first three months after sign-off to validate the process.

If you can incorporate those items into the addendum or MAP, we'll proceed to signature. We can accept the DocuSign timeline of next week if the addendum is updated.

Regards,
Lena Marsh
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Health - DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, CloudOps Backup Vendor <vendor-backups@cloudops.example.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: backup purge / archival grace for DPA mapping — mutual action plan

Lena — thanks, and appreciate the specificity. Below is a short mutual action plan (MAP) capturing agreed items and owners so procurement can move to signature. I've attached the MAP PDF with inline redlines for legal.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Finalize addendum: Kimberly to insert explicit log-type list and the 10-business-day audit-trigger language. (Owner: Kimberly Park) — Target: Nov 10
- Subprocessor attestation: Karhtik to coordinate with CloudOps for a signed attestation confirming region (us-east-1) and tenant-specific KMS usage. (Owner: Karthik Iyer) — Target: Nov 12
- Purge manifest exports: Engineering to enable monthly purge-manifest exports for first 90 days after sign-off, delivered to Acme security contacts. (Owner: Marissa Cole) — Target: First export within 30 days of signature
- DocuSign: Vanessa to issue updated DocuSign envelope once addendum updated. (Owner: Vanessa Ortiz) — Target: Nov 13

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-acme-backups.pdf (contains redlines and the revised 120d/180d language).

One final note on subprocessors: CloudOps has confirmed the current storage subprocessor list; Karhtik, can you confirm the signed attestation timeline?

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
